name: King of Jokneam
overview: The King of Jokneam was a male ruler identified as one of the thirty-one kings defeated by Joshua during the Israelite conquest. While his tribal affiliation and other personal details are not recorded, his defeat is noted as part of the broader military campaign led by Joshua. There are no additional personal notes or background information provided about him in Scripture.
namesAndTitles: The title 'King of Jokneam' simply identifies him as the reigning monarch of the city of Jokneam. The name means 'king of Jokneam' and does not carry a special theological or symbolic meaning beyond his political role. This title is recorded in Joshua 12:22.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for the King of Jokneam beyond his identification as a king defeated by Joshua. There are no known relatives or alliances mentioned in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of Jokneam is significant primarily as a representative of the Canaanite kings who opposed Israel during their divinely guided conquest of the Promised Land. His defeat under Joshua's leadership demonstrates God's faithfulness in granting Israel victory over established kingdoms. This event underscores the fulfillment of God's promises to His people and the establishment of Israel's possession of the land.
